messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: checking params & IEEE arithmetic
parts:
I was just adding a vectorized normal_log and
looked at what Daniel's been up to adding
error conditions. This is all on the right
track including the doc and error messages.

Unfortunately, we're going to need to change
the tests themselves, because IEEE isn't going
to do what you want in some of these cases.

The big problem is NaN, but the Inf cases can also be
problematic.

In particular, the condition under which we
want to raise an exception for a non-positive
scale parameter should be:

!(sigma > 0)

which, unlike for real numbers (or even computer
represented int) is NOT the same condition as:

sigma <= 0

If sigma is NaN, then (sigma <= 0) will fail, whereas
!(sigma > 0) will succeed. And we definitely want
to trap NaN errors.

In general, any built-in function or operator applied
to NaN will return NaN.

Any test with a NaN component will fail (except in
short-circuit boolean operators):

0.0 * NaN == NaN * 0 == NaN

(1 < NaN) == (1 > NaN) == (NaN > NaN) == false

((1 < 2) || (1 < NaN)) == true [short circuit]
((1 > 2) && (1 < NaN)) == false [short circuit]

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] checking params & IEEE arithmetic
parts:
Just so we're clear, the right behavior is for the distributions to
throw exceptions on NaN as input (when checking for errors).
I believe that is what Bob is stating and I agree.

Should we be checking all inputs for NaN? Even if we don't use them
for the calculation of the log probability?
